Keep identity distribution separate from relationship access

PathDistribution keyApproved payloadSeed behaviour
Global party minimumOwner + party UUIDid, global_party_id, party_typeAster: SG owner, GB and US recipients; Example Trading: US excluded.
Relationship graphOwner + relationship UUIDWhitelisted, dependency-closed rowsPersonal → LE-GB-02 contact; business → LE-GB-03 minimal; both exclude US.
Holding restrictionOwner + holding UUIDNarrowing rule on resource and childrenRestricted holding and its assignment are removed without dangling child references.
Global is an intent, not an exemption

A global party row remains identifying metadata. It requires explicit identity-resolution grants and approved physical placement. A shared global identity does not make a contact, relationship link, account identifier or product holding global. In this fixture three recipient grants illustrate all three physical stores; there is no blanket entitlement for all 30 entities.

The operational relationship model

Two parties, two relationships and three initial holdings form the seed graph. Aster is a personal account holder and an authorised business signatory; the organisation is the business account owner. The same party and contact resources participate in multiple scopes. Foreign keys preserve ownership at source and ownership, scope and recipient at the destination.

Source data remains operational

The business schema contains party, relationship, party_relationship, product_holding, contact_info, consent, preference, contact_history, three typed alternate-ID tables and classification. owner_entity_id represents business custody. Destination lists, country exclusions, policy versions and delivery receipts are separate. The classification table contains assignments with exactly one typed party/relationship/holding reference; a managed taxonomy catalogue is a future service.

Holding classified restrictedBusiness classification plus decision revisionOnly the affected holding and dependent rows are removed.
Coexistence with the earlier record sandbox

The original flat entity/customer records remain available for scenario generation. Their owner + global_customer_id key is a teaching fixture, not the normalized relationship key. New party and relationship scopes use independent UUIDs so several relationships for one party can coexist under the same legal entity.

Entity relocation decision: keep legal entity identity stable while changing physical home. Use a lawful transition policy, snapshot plus continuous change capture, versioned tombstones, target-applied checkpoints, graph closure and an entity-specific source writer fence. Persist source fencing before activating the target; never flip routing back after target writes. Separate placement version, writer epoch, policy revision and resource data version. Migration consumes the capped bulk lane; guard and operational capacity remain reserved. The executable edition-08 slice uses isolated mig_* row envelopes and one coordinator; it does not migrate the original normalized business.* fixture or prove distributed fencing. Read Entity relocation before implementation.

Extend the v3 operational PoC, preserving 30 legal entities and three independent single-node store models. Business data is normalized across 12 tables; sovereignty policies live in parallel control tables. A separate party scope exports only id/global_party_id/party_type; relationship scopes export connected whitelisted graphs. Global distribution still needs grants and approved geography; deny overrides. Do not infer relationship access from a global party, common store or shared identity. Keep the single local transaction and asynchronous destination acknowledgement distinct. The hosted UI is a labelled browser simulation. The unified Docker/CockroachDB/OPA suite and live Chromium generator/migration walkthrough passed. Database crash boundaries, accessibility and pilot load remain separate gates. Use synthetic data only. Deliver bounded adapters, actual migrations, meaningful invariant tests and honest run results.

Implement the typed relational model and independent party/relationship scopes. Preserve many-to-many party roles and three alternate-ID parent types. Bind shared resources without duplicating sovereignty flags into business rows. Test that US contains Aster’s party minimum but no relationship or contact, and that a party-key exclusion prevents even that minimum. Include model migrations and a graph fixture integrity validator.
